claims.statement: CTIS supplies searchable public trial facts and downloadable search or trial records, which is enough for a public-data prototype but not evidence of site-level startup, recruitment-delivery, query-burden, or closeout performance.

The EU clinical-trial transparency regime expressly protects personal data and commercially confidential information, so non-public operational outcomes require separate authority, contractual permissions, minimisation, and disclosure controls.

Published research supports startup speed, recruitment, patient access, and data quality as relevant site-selection or performance dimensions, but it does not validate one portable score or prove that Polish sites and CROs will share the required data.

Citeline, IQVIA, and Medidata already market sophisticated feasibility, site-selection, site-performance, workflow, and proprietary-data products, making generic site discovery or ranking an unattractive wedge.

It remains an unvalidated hypothesis that one CRO or sponsor will prepay a closed cohort, that invited sites will have usable sharing rights, and that repeat buyer use can support the existing pilot and annual price hypotheses.

contrary_evidence: Major vendors already advertise proprietary site-level performance, enrollment, quality, workflow, and API capabilities.
CTIS public records do not contain the private operational outcomes that would make the closed cohort valuable.
The published performance literature does not establish a fair cross-sponsor attribution method or willingness to fund a closed cohort.
No anchor commitment, site sharing right, repeat-use evidence, or public incumbent pricing was found.

economics.acquisition_route: Do not recruit an open site network. Use bounded founder-led outreach to seek one paid CRO or sponsor anchor; build only the scoped packet after prepayment, then invite only the sites required for that cohort. No anchor or site commitment is assumed.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: The prior path requiring 800 paying site accounts is removed. No founder-net-worth path is underwritten until a repeat-paid anchor establishes price, delivery cost, renewal, and expansion. Using only the prior planning ceiling of 100000 PLN annual buyer revenue and its 22% EBITDA, 4x EBITDA, and 60% ownership assumptions, roughly 95 retained anchor accounts would be required for about 5.0M PLN of equity, which exposes rather than resolves the scale risk; retained cash is not double-counted.
economics.founder_time: Keep the same 15-20 hour weekly ceiling, focused on one anchor sale, the bounded packet, and measurement; contract clinical-operations, privacy, and security work, and do not operate a broad site-support network.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Remove the unsupported 55-80% range from the launch decision. Measure specialist verification, security, site support, and dispute cost inside the prepaid pilot; an annual product is permitted only after positive contribution is observed.
economics.payback: Unknown. Require pilot prepayment within the already proposed 10000-25000 PLN scoped-packet range and size the scope so the fee covers budgeted direct pilot cost; stop rather than fund shared infrastructure if this cannot be contracted.
economics.pricing: Sites pay nothing. Test only the existing 10000-25000 PLN prepaid scoped-pilot range; after evidenced repeat use, test the existing 40000-100000 PLN annual buyer-access range. These are hypotheses and approval gates, not observed willingness to pay.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Repeat revenue is limited to additional studies and an annual renewal by the same anchor; site subscriptions and assumed contribution revenue are removed. Neither repeat use nor renewal is evidenced.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Permissioned longitudinal evidence produced under one buyer-agreed definition set, with provenance, sample thresholds, disclosure controls, and appeal history across repeat studies
fingerprint.customer: A mid-sized CRO or sponsor feasibility team with repeated Polish studies; independent sites participate in the closed cohort but are not paying customers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Bounded direct outreach to win one paid anchor first, followed only by anchor-nominated or explicitly invited sites; no open two-sided launch
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Pre-sold private evidence cohort for one therapeutic area, combining CTIS factual profiles with permissioned site evidence under anchor-agreed definitions, followed conditionally by an annual buyer-funded workflow
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The anchor CRO or sponsor prepays a scoped cohort pilot and, only after demonstrated repeat use, may pay annual access; sites pay nothing and no party pays to improve a rank
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A CRO or sponsor is preparing feasibility for a near-term Polish study and is willing to prepay a bounded cohort pilot before any shared infrastructure is built

founder_fit: One bounded pre-sale and cohort fits the founder's data-provenance and automation strengths better than operating an open two-sided exchange.
The design can be tested part-time and avoids a public persona, but still requires a finite enterprise sale.
Clinical-operations methodology, privacy, and security remain specialist work that must be contracted within the capital ceiling.
A no-build-before-prepayment gate contains downside while the decisive buyer and rights assumptions remain unknown.

redesign.economic_effect: This removes 800 assumed paying site accounts, site-side acquisition, and an open two-sided cold start. A single prepaid buyer pilot becomes the financing and demand gate, so shared build and site recruitment do not consume capital before revenue. The tradeoff is anchor concentration and a harder enterprise-only scale requirement; price, contribution, renewal, rights, and commitment remain explicitly unvalidated.

risks: No CRO or sponsor may prepay a site-controlled cohort when incumbents already own broader data and procurement access.
Invited sites may lack reuse rights or comparable records, leaving the paid scope undeliverable.
Anchor-specific definitions may not transfer across buyers, weakening expansion and the longitudinal asset.
Security review, verification, disputes, and enterprise sales may still exceed the founder's time and capital constraints.

structure.control_point: The private, permissioned cohort record and agreed evidence definitions used in repeat feasibility decisions
structure.critical_dependency: One buyer must prepay a bounded pilot and participating sites must possess and grant the required sharing rights; neither condition is currently evidenced

thesis: Pre-sell a closed, one-therapeutic-area evidence cohort to one CRO or sponsor before building shared infrastructure. The anchor funds a bounded feasibility pilot and agrees the evidence definitions; invited sites retain disclosure control and contribute only records they have authority to share. The product remains a private evidence packet and recurring cohort workflow, not a public score, open exchange, or claim that an anchor, contribution right, or buyer demand already exists.
title: Anchor-Funded TrialSite Evidence Cohort for Poland
uncertainties: Whether one CRO or sponsor will prepay a bounded closed-cohort pilot at the existing proposed range.
Whether invited sites possess contractual rights to share useful, comparable operating evidence.
Pilot delivery cost, contribution, decision impact, repeat use, renewal, and the number of anchors attainable without incumbent channel access.
Whether one anchor's definitions can transfer across therapeutic areas or buyers without recreating the service.
No anchor commitment, validation, rights confirmation, or improved economics is claimed.
